newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HIGHLIGHTS OF UEFA CUP FIRST ROUND SECOND LEG MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HIGHLIGHTS OF UEFA CUP FIRST ROUND SECOND LEG MATCHES.

text.p: Highlights of UEFA Cup first round second leg matches on Tuesday:
In Kerkrade, an early strike by Schalke's David Wagner dashed Dutch hopes that Roda JC could overturn a 3-0 first leg deficit against the German side.
After just quarter of an hour Wagner slotted into an empty net after Martin Max intercepted a back header by Roda defender Richard Roelofsen.
Roda, needing five goals to win the tie, scored 10 minutes later through Edwin Vurens but Schalke's Belgian striker Marc Wilmots made it 2-1 on the day in a breakaway attack in the 72nd minute.
Two minutes later Gerald Sibon pulled one back for Roda with a shot from an acute angle but Schalke go through 5-2 on aggregate and continue on their first European excursion for 19 years.
In Prague, headed goals by Martin Penicka and Robert Vagner in the opening half an hour set Czech champions Slavia Prague on their way to a 3-1 win over Malmo and a 5-2 aggregate victory.

Jens Fjellstrom pulled back a goal in the 56th minute but any hopes of a storming finish by the Swedish side were snuffed out when Pavel Horvath converted a 69th minute penalty after Jiri Vavra had been pulled down by Tommy Jonsson.
Herfried Sabitzer converted an 86th minute penalty against Belgian side Ekeren, his second goal of the match, to take Casino Graz of Austria into the second round on the away goals rule.
Casino Graz, 3-1 down from the first leg which ended with their Serbian coach Ljubo Petrovic resigning after physically attacking one of his players in the dressing room, won 2-0.
Sabitzer, who missed the first leg because of injury, had opened the scoring with a header in the 66th minute.
In Germany, SV Hamburg beat Glasgow Celtic 2-0 after a bad-tempered match in which Hamburg finished with 10 men and Celtic with nine.
Goals from Karsten Baron after 24 minutes and Andre Breitenreiter after 50 minutes gave Hamburg victory on the night and a 4-0 win on aggregate.

Celtic had Malky Mackay sent off for two bookings after 21 minutes and John Hughes sent off for two bookings just before halftime while Hamburg had Markus Schupp sent off in the 71st minute for a second bookable offence after a foul on Celtic's Danish substitute Morten Wieghorst.
Celtic also lost their top scorer, Portuguese striker Jorge Cadete, who was stretchered off after a dreadful foul by Hamburg defender Stephane Henchoz.
Celtic manager Tommy Burns was involved in a shouting match with the Russian referee Viktor Shuk at half-time following ugly scenes between both sets of players in the centre circle.
Celtic have now had six players sent off this season -- four in the last four matches.

Monaco, down to 10 men for almost half an hour, beat Hutnik Krakow of Poland 3-1 with two goals from Sonny Anderson, taking the Brazilian's tally to four in five days following a brace in Friday's league game against Le Havre.

The French first division side, who had defender Philippe Leonard sent off in the first leg, were one up from Anderson's 37th minute opener when captain Franck Dumas was shown the red card for stopping a shot from Wojciech Ozimek on the goal-line.
Substitute Waldemar Adamczyk converted the 64th minute penalty. But Monaco, having squandered a string of chances, completed a 4-1 aggregate victory with two goals in three minutes near the end.
Midfielder Lilian Martin curled a free kick into the top corner of the net in the 81st minute and Anderson dived to head home a rebound two minutes later.
Daniel Fonseca, whose two goals in Rome left Dynamo Moscow on the ropes in the first leg, finished the job in Russia with a coolly-taken penalty on the stroke of halftime.

The equaliser from Roma's Uraguayan international striker cancelled out a 19th minute Andrei Kobelev spot kick which had given the Russians a glimmer of hope of overcoming their 3-0 deficit from the away leg.

It left a dispirited Dynamo to spend the second half battering aimlessly at the solid Italian defence, opening the way for Damiano Tommasi and Daniele Berretta to add two more, humbling the Moscow side 3-1 on the night and 6-1 on aggregate.

The Italians clearly came to defend their lead, leaving Fonseca on lonely patrol up front. He saw little of the ball until, brought down with it in the 45th minute, he stepped up to take the resulting spot kick.
The job done, Fonseca came off at halftime, to be replaced by Abel Balbo.

A solitary goal by Cameroon defender Rigobert Song four minutes before the interval from a low cross from the left by winger Robert Pires was enough to give Metz a 1-0 aggregate win over Tirol Innsbruck.
The Austrians were down to 10 men for the last 10 minutes after captain Michael Streiter was sent off for a second bookable offence, a late tackle on French international Pires.
Just 300 fans watched Portuguese club Boavista reach the second round on the away goals rule at Benfica's 120,000-capacity stadium.
Boavista used Benfica's ground for their home leg against Denmark's Odense after being banned by UEFA from playing at their own ground in Oporto.
Two goals inside three minutes midway through the second half by Jasper Hjorth and Ulrik Pedersen gave Odense a 2-1 win on the night.
But the aggregate score of 4-4 left Boavista winners on the away goals rule.
In Rotterdam Feyenoord midfielder Kees van Wonderen scored his second goal of the tournament to dismiss CSKA Moscow.
Feyenoord took a 1-0 lead into the game after Van Wonderen, in his first season with the Dutch league leaders, scored in the first leg in Moscow.
But Valery Minko evened the tally in the 58th minute with a header through a disorganised Dutch defence.
Feyenoord brought in some more fire power with striker Henk Vos, who in the 73rd minute fired a fierce shot at goal which rebounded off the goalkeeper to offer Van Wonderen an easy chance.
Italy's Internazionale and Lazio eased into the second round despite being held to 1-1 draws at home by French clubs.
Inter, holding a commanding 3-0 lead over Guingamp from the first leg, went 4-0 up on aggregate when Marco Branco headed home in the seventh minute.
Christopher Wreh scored Guingamp's consolation goal in the 73rd minute.
Lazio also took a first-half lead against Lens, Diego Fuser scoring in the 43rd minute.
Lens's striker Smicer levelled the scores in the 67th minute but an uninspired Lazio held on to win 2-1 on aggregate.
Cezary Kucharski's injury time goal gave Legia Warsaw a place in the second round at the expense of Panathinaikos Athens.
Legia won their home leg 2-0, Marcin Mieciel scoring first in the 52nd minute, to level the scores 4-4 on aggregate. They qualified on the away goals rule.
